approachQuestion.prompt:
Release Orderings

Given n distinct jobs numbered 0 through n-1 and directed precedence edges (u,v), return every ordering in which u appears before v for each edge. Return each ordering once, in any order. If the constraints contain a cycle, return [].

Examples:
n=3, edges=[(0,2),(1,2)] -> [[0,1,2],[1,0,2]].
n=2, edges=[(0,1),(1,0)] -> [].

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 10; no repeated edges or self edges. Input is outgoing adjacency lists and an n-entry indegree array consistent with those lists.

options.text: Branch over every currently unused job with zero remaining indegree. Apply and undo its outgoing-edge decrements around the recursive call; emit only after all jobs are used.
options.feedback: The remaining indegree is relative to this prefix. Undoing exactly the chosen job’s changes preserves other branches; a shorter dead end is not a complete order.

options.text: Take only the smallest currently available job and return that one completed ordering.
options.feedback: The first example has two required answers; committing to job 0 first misses [1,0,2].

options.text: Decrease outgoing indegrees when choosing a job but never increase them on return.
options.feedback: For n=3, edges=[(0,2),(1,2)], returning from [0,1,2] leaves stale zero/negative counts; a sibling can admit job 2 before a prerequisite or lose legitimate availability.

options.text: Enumerate every permutation and check every precedence edge only on complete orders.
options.feedback: This is correct but extends prefixes that already place a job before an unplaced prerequisite; availability checks remove those branches.

feedback.reason: The remaining indegree is relative to this prefix. Undoing exactly the chosen job’s changes preserves other branches; a shorter dead end is not a complete order.
details: Copy indegrees. At each nonterminal call scan all n jobs. Choose each unused zero-indegree job, mark it used, decrement all outgoing neighbors, recurse, then restore those indegrees and the used mark. Copy the order at length n.

A choice temporarily removes its outgoing prerequisite contributions. Restore every decremented indegree on return so siblings see the same remaining graph. Copy only complete orders, not prefixes that become stuck.

“Branch over every currently unused job with zero remaining indegree. Apply and undo its outgoing-edge decrements around the recursive call; emit only after all jobs are used.”: The remaining indegree is relative to this prefix. Undoing exactly the chosen job’s changes preserves other branches; a shorter dead end is not a complete order.
“Take only the smallest currently available job and return that one completed ordering.”: The first example has two required answers; committing to job 0 first misses [1,0,2].

“Decrease outgoing indegrees when choosing a job but never increase them on return.”: For n=3, edges=[(0,2),(1,2)], returning from [0,1,2] leaves stale zero/negative counts; a sibling can admit job 2 before a prerequisite or lose legitimate availability.

“Enumerate every permutation and check every precedence edge only on complete orders.”: This is correct but extends prefixes that already place a job before an unplaced prerequisite; availability checks remove those branches.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-08-search` only. Let m be edge count, V count nonterminal recursive calls, E count all outgoing adjacency entries processed by decrements and restorations over the whole run, and R count copied job IDs. Each nonterminal call scans all n jobs. Initialization copies n indegrees. A terminal call copies n IDs. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n + n·V + E + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + V + E + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + n·V + E + R) time, O(n+m) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Explicit job scans, edge updates/undo, and output copies are separate cost terms.
details: The explicit scans perform n·V work, edge updates perform E work, and output copying performs R work. Root initialization adds n. Terminal call overhead is absorbed by R since n>=1.
Only n indegrees, n used flags, the current order and a depth-n stack are retained; adjacency lists are input.

Let m be edge count, V count nonterminal recursive calls, E count all outgoing adjacency entries processed by decrements and restorations over the whole run, and R count copied job IDs. Each nonterminal call scans all n jobs. Initialization copies n indegrees. A terminal call copies n IDs.
“O(n + V + E + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each nonterminal call scans every job, not only the currently available ones.
“O(n + n·V + E + R) time, O(n+m) auxiliary space”: The method uses the supplied adjacency lists without copying edges.
“O(n+m+R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Repeated scans and edge updates occur throughout a branching search, not once.
